r4a-park-diagnostic.title: Raising round parks with diagnostic reason and continues (no swallow-hide)
r4a-park-diagnostic.imperative: Confirm the try/except in run_season parks a raising round with a diagnostic reason (exception type+message) and CONTINUES; confirm it does NOT swallow-and-hide -- the parked round must be recorded in parked_rounds AND the rounds/results dict. Confirm the empty-grid park path is unchanged and remains distinguishable from the new run-failure park path.
r4a-park-diagnostic.finding: Direct source read (run_season_670.py:229-236): except Exception as exc sets rounds[circuit]={round_idx, status:'parked', reason:f'round failed at run_circuit: {type(exc).__name__}: {exc}'}, appends circuit to parked (-> parked_rounds in the returned dict), then continue -- season keeps iterating the slate. Not swallow-and-hide: the round IS recorded in both the per-round rounds dict (status+reason visible to any consumer) and the top-level parked_rounds list, satisfying the handoff's dual-recording requirement. Empty-grid park (lines 192-204) is untouched by this diff -- same reason text ('no session_classifications rows for ...'), taken in a separate branch BEFORE run_circuit_fn is ever called -- confirmed distinguishable from the run-failure reason ('round failed at run_circuit: ...') by both a manual read and the new test test_run_season_run_failure_park_distinguishable_from_empty_grid_park, which parks one round via each path in the same run and asserts on the differing reason substrings.

r4b-except-scope.title: except is scoped per-round, not around the whole loop
r4b-except-scope.imperative: Confirm the try/except is scoped to a single iteration's run_circuit_fn (+ check_round_vocabulary) call, inside the for-loop body -- not wrapping the whole loop -- so control returns to iterate the next slate entry rather than to a re-entry point outside the loop.
r4b-except-scope.finding: Confirmed by indentation/structure read: the for-loop is 'for circuit, round_idx in slate:' at line 191; the try: at line 206 and its except Exception at line 229 are BOTH indented one level inside that for-body (8 spaces vs the for's 4), i.e. the try/except wraps only run_circuit_fn+check_round_vocabulary for the CURRENT iteration, not the loop itself. The continue at line 236 returns control to the for statement to advance to the next slate entry -- if the except wrapped the whole loop instead, a raise would exit the loop entirely and no continue would be reachable inside it. The 3-round synthetic test (round 1 raises, rounds 2-3 succeed and are captured in order) directly proves iteration continued past the failure, which would be impossible under a whole-loop try/except.

r4c-tests-genuine.title: New tests genuinely exercise a raising round, not vacuous
r4c-tests-genuine.imperative: Confirm the new test(s) in tests/unit/physics/pilot/test_season_runner.py supply a run_circuit_fn that actually raises for one round and succeeds for others, and assert park+continue on real returned state (not a hardcoded/tautological assertion). Independently re-run with the pinned interpreter.
r4c-tests-genuine.finding: Read both new tests directly (lines 196-236 and 238-265). test_run_season_parks_round_that_raises_and_continues: flaky_run_circuit raises ValueError only for Bahrain, appends to a real 'captured' list + writes synthetic observables for the other two circuits; asserts result['rounds']['Bahrain']['status']=='parked', round_idx==1, 'ValueError' and 'no severity classes' both IN the reason (real exception message content, not a stub string), 'Bahrain' in parked_rounds, the OTHER two rounds are 'covered', and captured==['Saudi Arabia','Australia'] in order (proves the loop actually kept executing after the raise, not merely that the dict happens to contain the right keys). test_run_season_run_failure_park_distinguishable_from_empty_grid_park: one round takes the pre-existing empty-grid path (grid_reader returns () for round_idx==1) while flaky_run_circuit unconditionally raises RuntimeError('boom') -- both rounds park but assert on DIFFERENT reason substrings ('no session_classifications rows' vs 'RuntimeError'/'boom'/'run_circuit'), which would fail if the two paths were accidentally merged into one reason format. Neither test hardcodes the parked-round's reason text as a full-string equality (both use 'in' substring checks against the real f-string), so a future change to phrasing wouldn't silently pass a broken assertion, and a genuinely un-diagnostic reason (e.g. a bare 'error') would fail. Independently re-ran: pytest tests/unit/physics/pilot/test_season_runner.py -q -> 17 passed (both new tests execute and pass, no skip/xfail markers present on either). Not vacuous.
